A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReasonBreak and GeoPrivacy-6K research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, algorithms and complete Appendices A–G are readable and can be reliably matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original DoxBench evaluations across seven models, component ablations, qualitative analyses, timing measurements and JPEG compression experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–3 and the supplementary evaluations in Appendices C–G.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithms 1–4 retain the same adaptive decomposition, concept assignment, minimax prior selection, decoder architecture, ensemble loss and reconstruction procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 6,341-image GeoPrivacy-6K training collection, sourced from HoliCity, Aesthetic-4K and LHQ, and the same 500-image DoxBench evaluation. No dataset, task, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: AnyAttack and M-Attack remain the evaluated baselines in the performance, visual-quality and efficiency comparisons. The three newly cited works are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The seven target models, prompts, Top-1/Top-3 PPR metrics, four geographic granularities, perturbation budgets of 8/255 and 16/255, and training settings are unchanged. Appendix G retains JPEG quality factors 95, 75 and 50.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same noise-budget analysis, decomposition and minimax ablations, OCR failure cases, prompt-sensitivity example, visual-quality analysis and JPEG robustness test. Appendix analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for protection performance. Figure 7's annotation-confidence distributions and the discussion of output randomness are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical values, including GPT-o3 Top-1 tract PPR of 31.7% and InternVL 3.0 72B Top-1 block PPR of 58.3% in Table 1. Scaling curves, ablation findings, Appendix F timings and qualitative results also match.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and Section 4.2's formulation of conceptual and sequential dependencies are unchanged. No mathematical definition, assumption, derivation or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about disrupting hierarchical geographic reasoning, contributing GeoPrivacy-6K and outperforming baselines across seven models. The headline protection rates and contribution scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of concept entanglement, fragmentation, inverted scaling and input sensitivity are unchanged. Section 5.5 retains the limitation concerning direct OCR-based location identification, and the appendices retain the same applicability interpretations.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, architecture details, annotation instructions, hardware requirements, timings and release promises remain unchanged. The abstract relabels the project-page link but retains the same destination, without providing new access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Liu et al. (2024, Pandora's Box), Cai et al. (2025) and Fang et al. (2026). This modestly expands citation coverage without developing new comparisons or revising the novelty argument.

P1.justification: v2 adds a funding acknowledgment and corresponding-author footnote, updates the publication header, relabels the project link and makes small grammatical and wording edits in Sections 3.3–4.1. The scientific narrative and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 compacts the affiliations, reduces the displayed sizes of Figures 2 and 5, and adjusts text and float placement. The conclusion fits on page 10 and references shift appendix pagination; all ten figures and three tables retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 adds three citations without further comparative discussion, along with funding/contact disclosures and light copyediting and layout adjustments. These provide modest editorial polish but leave the explanatory substance, empirical support, reproducibility information and stated limitations essentially unchanged, producing no meaningful overall quality difference.
